excerpt: A Risk Report will cover the risks of Anthropic's models and actions as of a given coverage date, which will be no more than 30 days prior to the publication of the report.
paraphrase: Each Risk Report covers risks as of a coverage date no more than 30 days before publication.

excerpt: It will cover all publicly deployed models as of the coverage date, as well as any internally deployed models as of the coverage date that, by the time of the report's publication, we have determined (1) could pose risks related to high-stakes misalignment or automated R&D that (2) significantly exceed those posed by models covered by a prior Risk Report.
paraphrase: Coverage includes all publicly deployed models and internal models newly determined to pose significantly greater misalignment or automated R&D risk than previously covered models.

excerpt: While there are a variety of reasons we might classify an internal model this way, this will—at a minimum—include any internal models that we are deploying for large-scale, fully autonomous research.
paraphrase: At minimum, internal models deployed for large-scale fully autonomous research will be classified as in-scope.

excerpt: Models fitting the above description are abbreviated below as "in-scope models."
paraphrase: Qualifying models are termed in-scope models.

excerpt: We may also voluntarily include additional models in a Risk Report, e.g., to contribute to general discourse, but such inclusion does not expand the commitments below.
paraphrase: Additional models may voluntarily be included without expanding stated commitments.

excerpt: We will publish a Risk Report every 3-6 months.
paraphrase: Risk Reports will be published every 3-6 months.

excerpt: Note that unlike system cards, Risk Reports will not be published with each new model release.
paraphrase: Risk Reports differ from system cards in not being published per model release.

excerpt: Separate from our publication of Risk Reports, we will publish an analysis of an individual model's relevant risks (e.g., how the model's capabilities and propensities affect or change prior analyses) in the following circumstances:
paraphrase: Anthropic will publish standalone risk analyses for individual models under certain circumstances, apart from Risk Reports.

context_stem: Separate from our publication of Risk Reports, we will publish an analysis of an individual model's relevant risks in the following circumstances:
excerpt: When we publicly deploy a model that we determine is (1) significantly more capable than (2) all models for which we have publicly analyzed risks related to chemical/biological weapons production, high-stakes misalignment, or automated R&D (e.g., in a prior Risk Report, System Card, or other public artifact).
paraphrase: An off-cycle analysis is triggered when a publicly deployed model is significantly more capable than all previously publicly analyzed models on relevant risks.

excerpt: A Risk Report may include information about Anthropic's models and risk preparedness more recent than the coverage date, but does not guarantee completeness about such information.
paraphrase: Risk Reports may include more recent information but do not guarantee its completeness.

context_stem: Separate from our publication of Risk Reports, we will publish an analysis of an individual model's relevant risks in the following circumstances:
excerpt: Within 30 days of determining that we have an internally deployed model that (1) could pose risks related to high-stakes misalignment or automated R&D that (2) significantly exceed those of all models for which we have publicly analyzed such risks (e.g., in a prior Risk Report, System Card, or other public artifact).
paraphrase: An off-cycle analysis must be published within 30 days of determining an internal model significantly exceeds prior publicly analyzed risk levels.

excerpt: Several principles guide how we approach Risk Reports:
paraphrase: Introductory statement to a list of guiding principles for Risk Reports.

context_stem: Several principles guide how we approach Risk Reports:
excerpt: We intend for our Risk Reports to be direct, candid, and informative about how we see the risks of our systems and our state of preparedness for them.
paraphrase: Anthropic intends Risk Reports to be direct, candid, and informative.

context_stem: Several principles guide how we approach Risk Reports:
excerpt: In particular, we will acknowledge when we view certain models as posing significant risks in absolute terms, even if our marginal contribution to overall ecosystem risk may be relatively limited when taking other developers' AI models into account.
paraphrase: Anthropic will acknowledge significant absolute risk even where its marginal contribution to ecosystem risk is limited.

context_stem: Several principles guide how we approach Risk Reports:
excerpt: We will put significant effort into investigating (for example, via capability evaluations) the case for risk, and into sharing what we find.
paraphrase: Anthropic will invest significant effort in investigating and sharing risk findings.
